facilities.geo_note: Geocoded from street address via NSW Spatial Services address point for 105 HOLLINSWORTH ROAD MARSDEN PARK (113 Hollinsworth Rd is at -33.72446,150.83675). Address point, not building centroid; campus spans a larger lot.
facilities.mw_note: EIS Figure 16 GFA table lists 'Development 1 (79MW)' and s3.1 describes 'the 79MW Data Centre building, referred to as MP1 Development - Stage 2 (MP1.S2)'. The separate 5 MW MP1.S1 building (Blacktown DA-24-00542, source 26/27) sits beside it and connects to MP01 via skybridge; MP1.S1 + MP1.S2 = 84 MW. Built's CEMP (source 28) describes all six buildings as 84 MW. CDC Mar 2026 investor day (source 16, snippet) says campus now 700MW+ after densification, so per-building IT may rise.
facilities.mw_grid_note: Approximate. EIS infrastructure section: 'The calculated demand for the site is approx. 720MW, made up of six (6) similar buildings (circa 120MW each)'. Consent (source 24) approves 'a maximum power consumption of 720 megawatts' for the campus (AR: '720 MW (504 MW IT load)').
facilities.cost_note: CAMPUS TOTAL capital investment value for all six SSD buildings (not broken down per building): EDC $3,113,226,273 excl GST ($3,424,550,000 incl GST) per Rider Levett Bucknall EDC letter 30 Oct 2024 (source 22), EIS, Assessment Report and notice of decision; ministerial release rounds to $3.1 billion. SEARs-stage figure was AU$1.4bn (source 7). The 5 MW MP1.S1 building under Blacktown DA-24-00542 had a separate CIV of $53,940,000 (source 27).
facilities.builder_note: Built Pty Ltd is Principal/Head Contractor for the SSD campus works per its CEMP (source 28, approved by DPHI Apr 2026) and its 14 Jul 2026 commencement notice (source 29); BY Group is head contractor for civil, stormwater and erosion control. This covers MP1.S2 (the 79 MW SSD building). The separate 5 MW MP1.S1 building (Blacktown DA-24-00542) was reportedly built by Hindmarsh Constructions (iCost AU$65m package, source 11, search extract only; iCost page now returns 404, not verified).

jobs_c.note: CAMPUS TOTAL (all six SSD buildings). EIS s3.1.1: 'CDC's Construction Operations team has identified that the proposal would generate up to a peak maximum of 220 construction workers during the life of the project, with an average of 150 construction workers.' EIS Table 6, application form (source 21) and Assessment Report (source 23) describe the same number as 'Up to 220 full-time equivalent (FTE) construction jobs' / '220 full-time equivalent construction jobs'; ministerial release: '220 construction jobs'.

jobs_c_other.note: CAMPUS TOTAL. EIS s3.1.1: '...with an average of 150 construction workers.'

CAMPUS TOTAL. Information Age: 'The NSW government has said the new data centre will create 200 construction jobs and 265 operational jobs'; conflicts with the ministerial release and planning documents (220), likely a reporting error.
CAMPUS TOTAL. CDC ground-breaking release 25 Oct 2024: 'The campus development will generate over ten thousand jobs' (lower bound, undefined; not comparable with planning figures).

jobs_o.note: CAMPUS TOTAL at full operation, including the 5 MW MP1.S1 building. EIS s3.1.1: 'the proposal is expected to generate 265 FTE operational jobs'; Table 7 'Forecast Operational Employment Generation Across Campus' totals 265 = office staff 132, security 33, visitors 35, contractor 65 (so includes visitors). Assessment Report/consent: '265 operational jobs'.

jobs_o_other.note: PER BUILDING, stated by source. EIS Table 7 '84MW Typical' building: office staff 20, security 5, visitors 5, contractor 10 = 40. MP1.S2 is a 79 MW building; table does not give a 79 MW column.

5 MW MP1.S1 building only (DA-24-00542). Council assessment report s8.2.3: 'the applicant only proposes 25 staff and maximum 5 visitors to attend this facility.' EIS Table 7 '5MW (inc. gatehouse)' column also totals 25 (12 office, 3 security, 5 visitors, 5 contractor).
CAMPUS TOTAL. Assessment Report (traffic): 'car parking supply has been provided based on employee demand of 165 staff and excess for site visitors' (parking-demand basis).

facilities.builder_note: No data centre builder. BESS designed/procured/built by Quinbrook affiliate Private Energy Partners (source 9).
